html:
"Zhoa" on the map is almost certainly a misspelling of Zhou, the people and dynasty of the Wei River valley in northwest China. The map shows it in 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE; the chart's Zhou bar covers the dynasty.

Before 1046 BCE the Zhou were a western people on the edge of the Shang world. Around 1046 BCE King Wu defeated the last Shang king and founded the dynasty. To justify it the Zhou taught the Mandate of Heaven: Heaven gives the right to rule to the virtuous and takes it from the wicked.

The Western Zhou ruled through relatives and allies who were given land to govern. In 771 BCE invaders sacked their capital and the court moved east to Luoyang. After that the king's power faded, and real power passed to the states of the Spring and Autumn period and then the Warring States. Confucius looked back to the early Zhou as a golden age. The Qin ended the last Zhou line in 256 BCE.
